criteria_quotes: Procedure is indicated for 1 or more of the following: Rotator cuff injury, as indicated by 1 or more of the following:

Acute full-thickness injury, as indicated by 1 or more of the following: Massive rotator cuff tear; New inability to externally rotate arm against resistance; Inability to elevate arm on physical examination (ie, pseudoparalysis); Disabling limitation of function in affected arm
Acute partial-thickness injury due to trauma refractory to nonoperative therapy (eg, NSAIDs, physical therapy) for at least 3 months

Chronic partial-thickness or full-thickness injury that requires repair, as indicated by ALL of the following: Symptomatic (ie, pain or significant functional impairment); Lack of sufficient improvement after at least 6 weeks of nonoperative therapy (eg, NSAIDs, physical therapy)
Irreparable injury and planned arthroscopic balloon placement
Revision of prior rotator cuff repair
answer.submission_route:
You can submit your appeal in several ways:
1. Online (Fastest): Log into your InTouch for Members account (https://intouch.pacificsource.com) and select 'Ask a Question' to securely upload your Member Appeal Form and supporting clinical documentation.
2. Email: Send the completed form and clinical documents to NewAppeal@PacificSource.com.
3. Fax: Fax your appeal documents to (541) 225-3628.
4. Mail: Send to PacificSource Health Plans, Appeal and Grievance Department, P.O. Box 7068, Springfield, OR 97475-0068.
For questions or to request an expedited 72-hour review, call Customer Service at (888) 977-9299.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: PacificSource utilizes third-party clinical criteria from MCG Health (Milliman Care Guidelines) for standard shoulder/orthopedic surgeries. Since these guidelines are proprietary, they are not fully published on the main PacificSource website. If you wish to obtain a copy of the specific criteria applied to your denial directly from the payer, you can contact PacificSource Customer Service at (888) 977-9299 or request them in writing through your secure InTouch member portal.
answer.notes: PacificSource does not publish its own proprietary, self-branded medical policy for standard arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827). Instead, they contract with MCG Health to use their evidence-based guidelines. The criteria quoted above represent the standard MCG criteria for shoulder arthroscopy (S-1045) which govern CPT 29827. To build a strong appeal, the patient's provider should supply clinical records detailing whether the tear is acute or chronic, physical therapy/NSAID trial duration (minimum 6 weeks for chronic, 3 months for acute partial-thickness), and clear functional limitations or pain levels.
